headline: Sensex and Nifty tumble as RBI's hawkish stance and rising crude prices trigger a sharp selloff

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: RBI's calibrated tightening stance and hawkish monetary policy tone
Rising Brent crude oil prices, which increased by 2% to impact sentiment
Global foreign outflows from emerging markets as the US Fed turns hawkish
Market jitters ahead of corporate earnings and domestic economic policy shifts
whatHappening: BSE Sensex plummeted over 600 points, reaching its lowest level of the day
NSE Nifty 50 broke below the 22,350 mark during the morning session
The India VIX volatility index surged by 5% amid the broad market selloff
IT stocks bucked the trend, trading higher ahead of TCS's quarterly results
summary: Indian markets faced a sharp downturn on October 8, with the Sensex and Nifty falling significantly due to the RBI's hawkish stance. Rising crude oil prices and foreign capital outflows from emerging markets further dampened investor sentiment across most sectors. While IT stocks showed resilience ahead of TCS results, increased volatility and a 5% jump in the VIX highlighted market caution.
